Play report

I reached level 5 of 6 and did not beat the game. Levels 1–4 are beaten; the game ended with GAME_OVER partway through level 5 when the action budget ran out.

**How the game works:**
- Actions 1–4 move a block up, down, left and right; the block faces the direction it last moved. The goal is to move it into a box with a blue border.
- Each level shows one or more small pattern panels. Clicking the cells of a 3×3 panel at the bottom to match a pattern triggers that pattern's effect:
  - **Cross pattern:** shrinks the block from 4×4 to 2×2, so it fits through narrow passages.
  - **Diagonal/corner pattern:** teleports the block to an area marked on the map.
  - **Middle-column pattern:** fires a projectile in the facing direction. Hitting a switch box opens the matching coloured barrier.
- A bar on the right edge fills as you act, and the game ends when it is full.

**Level 5:** I opened the first gate with a shot, crossed into the second room, shrank the block, climbed up and shot the second switch, which opened the last barrier before the goal. The final teleport would have been followed by about 8 moves up to the goal. On the third and last click of that teleport, the action bar filled and the game ended.

**Why it failed:** I misjudged the cost of actions. From the bar's fill, moves seemed to cost about one unit each, but clicks on the panel appear to cost about twice that. My route used more clicks than it could afford. I have not called reset; the game is over and waiting.

Round interview

**1. What happened on level 5**

The level has three linked areas. The block starts in a lower-left room. A gate (colour c) separates that room from a lower-right room. The goal sits in a closed-off corridor at the top, and that corridor is blocked by a second barrier (colour d). Each barrier opens when a projectile hits its switch box. You fire by clicking the "shoot" pattern into the 3×3 panel. You reach the goal corridor only by clicking the "teleport" pattern. The switch for the top barrier can only be hit from a narrow upper passage, which the block can only enter after the "shrink" pattern makes it 2×2.

I did all of that in order: shot the first switch, crossed the gate, shrank, climbed, shot the second switch. On the third and last click of the teleport pattern, the action bar on the right edge filled and the game ended. About 7–8 moves to the goal were still left.

The cause was budget. Panel clicks clearly cost more of the bar than moves. My readings of the bar suggest a move costs about 1 of its 64 rows and a click about 2.5–3.4 rows. I didn't measure this before committing. My route needed 13 clicks and about 28 moves, which is over budget.

**2. Can it be beaten?**

I think so, but I haven't checked it. My route was roughly 8–9 move-units over budget. Without new information, I can only trim about 3 moves:
- Climb in the lower-right room as a 4×4 block (two moves) before shrinking, instead of climbing as a 2×2 block.
- Stop one move earlier at the goal, since earlier levels counted touching its interior as a win.

That isn't enough on its own, so beating the level rests on an assumption I haven't tested. Each room has a 2×2 coloured item I ignored:
- an **e-coloured** item in the lower-right room, close to my route. e is the colour of the action bar, so I suspect it refills the bar.
- an **f-coloured** item in the lower-left room. f is the shrink colour, so it may be a free shrink.

Two things would settle it:
- What these items do when the block touches them.
- An exact cost per move and per click, read from the bar one action at a time.

If neither item helps and clicks really cost about 3 rows, I believe the level can't be done within the budget.

**3. Next attempt**

- Record the bar after every action to pin down the cost of a move and of a click.
- Follow the same route with the savings above.
